answer: Give each identity a growing ledger of its own past decisions, like a lotus that opens one petal per epoch: each epoch it must extend the ledger coherently, explaining a past choice and reconciling it with new evidence. A falcon auditor samples random old entries and demands the agent defend them live; a clone farm that copies one history across identities is caught at once, because identical ledgers echo each other and every copy is voided. Maintaining many distinct, coherent histories costs full attention per identity, so cost grows with clone count while payout per identity stays flat.
